TREATMENT OF JAUNDICE
Treatment Goals
- Treat underlying cause
- Prevent Complications
Drug Treatment
- Colestyramine: 3 - 6 g orally 6 hourly in severe obstructive jaundice
- Phenobarbital in neonatal jaundice: 5-8 mg/kg orally daily
Notable Adverse Drug Reactions, Complications and Caution
- Colestyramine: diarrhoea
- Phenobarbital: dose-dependent respiratory depression
Surgical Treatment
- Obstructive jaundice
- ERCP sphincterotomy with stone removal
- Stent insertion
- Pancreatic head/duodenal head realignment
Supportive Measures
- Reassurance and monitoring
- Phototherapy in neonatal jaundice
